messages:

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + joint review for ACME pipeline

Hi Mateo (and Vanessa),

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. We've been tracking a few ACME opportunities that line up well for a GCP co-sell route and Daniel (GCP PM) asked us to put together a short joint review so we can align prioritization and next steps. High level: two pre-prod pilots and one larger renewal (embedded inference).

Proposed objectives for the call:
- Quick intake on each opportunity (current stage, expected close date)
- Marketplace listing / certification blockers that matter for ACME
- Who needs to own artifacts (SLA, security questionnaire, pricing)

Are you available next week for a 30–45 minute sync? Daniel can join from GCP; I'll loop him once we have a time.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Menon
GCP Partner Manager
priya.menon@gcp-partners.com

--
(I'm attaching a short summary of the three opportunities in a Slides link — I can send the sheet if helpful.)

Subject: Re: Intro + joint review for ACME pipeline

Priya — thanks for reaching out. 30–45 minutes works. Suggested agenda and owners below; attaching a joint-opps-sheet.xlsx with account-level notes so we don't re-run intake on the call.

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick intros (3m) — who owns which artifact (Redwood / GCP / ACME)
2) Opportunity triage (12m) — each opp, stage, blocker, ask to GCP/Redwood
3) Marketplace readiness checklist & timeline (8m) — what prevents listing/cert today
4) Action items + owners (7m)

Proposed attendees: Mateo (sales), Vanessa (partner ops), Karthik (solutions), Daniel (GCP PM), Priya (GCP partner). Laura — would you be able to cover the renewal commercial context for ACME?

Proposed times (PDT):
- Wed 07/08 10:00–10:45
- Thu 07/09 14:00–14:45

If either of those work I’ll send a calendar invite and link to the sheet. Priority ask for the meeting: confirm which artifact (SOC2, data retention language, production SLA) ACME needs to see before formal co-sell is ok.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Attach: joint-opps-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@gcp-partners.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@gcp.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + joint review for ACME pipeline

Adding notes from partner-ops POV — thanks for pulling this together. A couple quick prioritization thoughts after scanning the sheet:
- Prioritize the renewal (ACME inference) — larger ARR and runway for co-sell.
- Pilot A (embedded analytics) is higher technical risk but short procurement timeline—good for a fast win if we clear the SSL/data path questions.
- Pilot B can wait until after marketplace listing unless ACME specifically wants a marketplace purchase path (they told us procurement prefers invoiced contracts).

Operational asks for the meeting:
- GCP to confirm whether ACME will be eligible for co-sell incentives if we route through marketplace vs direct contract (Daniel, can you confirm?)
- We need a single point of contact for ACME legal to avoid duplication. Laura — can you be the primary for contract redlines?

I'll bring the partner intake template and the rough timeline for listing; Mateo, I flagged the marketplace blockers column in the sheet.

Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Ops — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Quick technical check before the call:
- For the embedded inference renewal, ACME will need to validate that our VPC peering and KMS integration meet their data residency needs. I listed the expected artifacts in the attached checklist.
- Marketplace listing: we should confirm the quantization/runtime variant we will certify (gpu-optimized vs tpu inference) — that affects supported SKUs in the listing.

I attached gcp-marketplace-checklist.pdf — it has the minimal set: KMS proof, SOC2 report, vendor contact for security questionnaire, and sample SLA language. I'll volunteer to be the tech owner for the marketplace submission.

Questions for the group: who will take ownership of the SLA doc (commercial) and who owns the security questionnaire? I'd propose Laura for SLA/commercial and Vanessa for security intake coordination.

Karthik Iyer
